texts.zh:
[from.GetName]这些异常的地质扫描结果的根源是一群游荡的硅基巨型动物群。

这些巨大的生物长距离迁徙，周期性地潜入行星的熔岩湖中获取喜欢的食物：一种富含易爆微粒的岩质沉淀物。通过追踪它们的迁徙路径，我们就能在对行星的生态系统造成极低的影响下提取这些沉淀为自己所用。

它们厚重的外骨骼可以抵御极端温度；对这些生物生命周期进行更详尽深入的研究可以产出惊人的结果。
texts.en:
The anomalous tectonic scans on [from.GetName] have been attributed to the presence of large herds of roaming silicon-based megafauna.

Migrating across great distances, these enormous creatures periodically submerge in the planet's lava lakes to gather their preferred food source: a rocky sediment rich in Volatile Motes. By tracking their migratory patterns, we will be able to extract these sediments for our own needs with minimal impact to the planet's ecosystem.

Their thick outer carapaces are able to withstand extreme temperatures; a deeper, more detailed study of their life cycle could yield fascinating results.

texts.zh:
对[from.From.GetName]上独特的大型动物进行研究得出了一种可转用的热动力学洞见，能应用在我们的船舶工业中。

这种生物摄入的微粒使他们的外壳上形成了一种基于重质硅酸盐的结构，并得到天然存在的难熔金属的补强。

从它们脱落的外壳上取回无数的样本之后，我们的[Root.Owner.GetEngineerPlural]现在可以复制这种生物力学原理，用于研发我们自己的船体镀层。
texts.en:
Comprehensive study of the unique megafauna on [from.From.GetName] has revealed transferable thermodynamic insights which can be applied within our shipyards.

The mote-infused diet of the creatures results in a heavy silicate-based structure forming throughout their durable outer shells, reinforced with naturally occurring refractory materials.

Having recovered numerous samples of their shedded outer layers, our [Root.Owner.GetEngineerPlural] can now replicate their biomechanical principles in the development of our own hull platings.

texts.zh:
[from.GetName]上的大型动物能抵御熔融星球上的极端环境，深深潜入行星上无数熔岩池之中。

研究这些生物的甲壳可能帮助我们理解如何抵御极端热量。
texts.en:
The megafauna on [from.GetName] are able to withstand the harsh environments of their molten world, and submerge themselves deep below the surface of the planet's numerous magma pools.

Studying these creatures' carapaces may give us a new understanding of how to deal with extreme heat.
